items.headline: Suno Inks ‘Strategic Partnership’ With Believe
items.excerpt: AI music platform Suno has signed a strategic partnership with French music giant Believe, adding another major distributor to the licensed side of its business. The deal extends Suno's push to build industry-sanctioned models and revenue paths for artists even as it fights copyright suits elsewhere.

items.headline: Armin van Buuren and Laidback Luke Partner With ‘Responsible’ AI Music Company Moises
items.excerpt: Trance stars Armin van Buuren and Laidback Luke have partnered with Moises, an AI music company that positions itself around consent-based, artist-approved models. The tie-up puts working producers' voices and stems into the loop of how AI production tools are trained and used.

items.headline: Jason Isbell Files Class Action Lawsuit Claiming Suno Coded AI to ‘Extract Musicians’ Identities’
items.excerpt: Jason Isbell filed a class action against Suno accusing the platform of designing its generator to evoke identifiable artists' vocal and stylistic characteristics. The suit shifts the fight from training data to the output side — whether a model can legally sound like a specific human performer.

items.headline: Latest Suno lawsuit accuses AI company of violating the publicity rights of musicians rather than infringing their copyrights
items.excerpt: A group of musicians claim Suno violated their US publicity rights by "encoding musicians' identities into its AI model" — a legal theory that sidesteps copyright entirely. If it lands, it would put a new constraint on what generative music models are allowed to imitate.

items.headline: Donald Trump’s DoJ says OpenAI should be able to do whatever it wants with copyright protected works
items.excerpt: The US Department of Justice intervened in the New York Times v OpenAI case to argue that AI training is fair use under American copyright law. The position would directly weaken the music industry's central argument in its own suits against Suno and Udio.

items.headline: Stella Parton urges people to stop creating AI ‘endless garbage’ about her late sister Dolly
items.excerpt: Stella Parton has publicly asked people to stop generating AI images, songs and stories about her late sister Dolly Parton. Her appeal is a reminder that posthumous likeness is now the most exposed surface in AI music culture.

items.headline: Roland releases Melody Flip, a FREE AI-assisted songwriting plugin
items.excerpt: Roland has released Melody Flip, a free AI-assisted songwriting plugin for macOS and Windows built on technology developed with Sony Computer Science Laboratories. It analyses a musical reference and generates melody, chord, bass and drum variations you can export as MIDI and finish in your DAW.

items.headline: SoundBoost updates its browser-based mastering service with Engine v4
items.excerpt: SoundBoost's Engine v4 lets you steer a master with plain-language instructions instead of assembling a mastering chain by hand. It renders a three-minute track in roughly ten seconds and accepts iterative refinement requests without restarting the job.
